title: Activation signal protocol and bottleneck sherpa
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a tactical, lightweight protocol to map go/no-go signals for mid-sized feature activations and a short playbook for detecting and smoothing bottlenecks during ramp. Goal is to give on-call product ops, SRE, and release owners a single page to run from during prelaunch -> 72h post-activation.

Scope:
- Surface-level checks and KPIs (not deep load-testing plans).
- Applies to staged activations (canary -> 25% -> 100%) for API-backed features and model-serving changes.
- Not a replacement for runbooks owned by SRE or infra (links included).

TL;DR (one-line):
If latency or error budget crosses thresholds OR customer-facing adoption drops relative to expected cohort by >20% within a staging slice, pause traffic and escalate to SRE + Product on-call.

Activation signal board (quick reference):
- Phase: Canary (1–2% traffic) | Primary owner: Release PM | Expected observation window: 60m
  - Success if: 95th p50 latency <= baseline + 50ms AND error rate <= baseline * 1.3
  - Abort if: error rate > baseline * 2 OR 95th p50 latency > baseline + 200ms for >5 consecutive 5m windows
- Phase: Ramp (10–25%) | Owner: Product Ops + SRE | Window: 4 hours
  - Success if: token-cost per call, tail latency, and DB QPS all within targets
  - Abort if: sustained increase in user-visible failures, or degraded KPI signal trends (see KPI tracker below)
- Phase: Full (100%) | Owner: Eng Lead + Product Ops | Window: 24–72 hours
  - Watch for emergent performance regressions and user-feedback volume spikes

KPI tracker (short list to watch during activation) — track at slice level and aggregate:
- Uptime / availability (per route): target 99.95%
- API error rate (5xx): target <0.2% (canary margin allowed up to 0.5%)
- 95th percentile latency (in ms): target baseline + 100ms for canary, baseline + 50ms for ramp
- Cost per 1k tokens / inference (USD): expected delta <= +15% vs baseline for first 24h
- Key user flows success rate (end-to-end): target 98%
- Customer support mentions (volume): baseline + 2x in first hour -> immediate review
- Adoption delta (new users completing flow vs expected): warn at -10%, abort at -20%

How to measure baselines quickly:
- Use last 7-day rolling median for latency and error rate, excluding known incidents (tagged).
- For cost, use model/instance-level cost-per-token metric from billing dashboard snapshot 24h before activation.
- For adoption, use cohort of control bucket traffic from feature flags.

Readiness checklist (pre-activation, quick pass):
- [ ] Traffic split configured in feature flags with rollback toggle (owner: FE Eng)
- [ ] Canary script + synthetic jobs scheduled (owner: SRE)
- [ ] Alert rules created and pointed to on-call (owner: Product Ops)
- [ ] Runbook links included in Slack playbook (owner: Release PM)
- [ ] Key dashboards pinned and shared to #product-activation (owner: Observability)
- [ ] Customer comms template ready for first 24h (owner: CS)
- [ ] Postmortem template pre-created (owner: Eng Lead)

Bottleneck detection heuristics (fast checks):
- If queue depth or pending requests on gateway increases >50% vs baseline while CPU stays flat -> likely thread/queue starvation on worker (tag for SRE).
- Rising tail latency but stable p50 -> KV-cache misses or cold-starts; check cache hit ratio and instance scaling events.
- Cost per token spike with normal latency -> model fallback or longer-context calls being routed; inspect route routing logs and model variant table.
- DB latency correlated with specific feature endpoints -> run slow query collector and compare to migration/PR windows.

Escalation ladder (who to call, in order):
1) Product Ops on-call (Slack + phone)
2) SRE on-call (pager)
3) Serving runtime lead (pager)
4) Release PM and Eng Lead (phone)
4) CS lead (for customer impact comms)

Playbook for a detected abort signal (quick play):
- Step 0: Pause new traffic to feature flag slice (Product Ops)
- Step 1: Post status in #product-activation with short summary + runbook link (Product Ops)
- Step 2: SRE triages metric set: traces, instance CPU/memory, queue depth, DB slow queries (SRE)
- Step 3: If root cause is config/rolling deploy, roll back to previous model/version (Release PM + Eng)
- Step 4: If root cause is capacity, trigger emergency autoscale policy or shift traffic to fallback region/model (SRE + Infra)
- Step 5: Communicate to affected customers (CS) and schedule immediate postmortem if outage >30m

Notes to self / open questions:
- Need a quick synthetic that runs a representative multi-step chat flow (task: Marcello)
- Add a small dashboard card for cost-per-1k-tokens by model-variant (owner: Observability)
- Validate that private deployments' rollout tooling supports same feature-flag API (owner: Private Deployments)

Post-activation 72h checklist (owner: Release PM):
- [ ] Aggregate signal review (latency, errors, adoption) and mark pass/fail per slice
- [ ] If pass: schedule follow-up 2-week performance review (quantize costs and accuracy)
- [ ] If fail: start incident-lifecycle play (root cause & remediation backlog)
- [ ] Capture notes and tag linked artifacts (Confluence page, Jira ticket)

Appendix: quick commands / queries (examples we use in run):
- Error rate: SELECT count(*)/total FROM requests WHERE status >= 500 AND ts > now()-interval '1 hour' GROUP BY 5m
- 95th latency: use tracing service prefixed query "service.web.requests.p95" by route and slice

This document is intentionally lean — use for fast decisions during a rollout. If this flow proves useful, we will fold the core check rules into the activation-signal pipeline and a templated dashboard.

Last notes: Drafted in collaboration with Marcello (SRE) and Tess (Obs). Would like feedback from Release PMs on the adoption thresholds — they look conservative for mobile-first launches.
